newsitem.title: USA: US fund managers raise cash a tad higher - survey.
newsitem.headline: US fund managers raise cash a tad higher - survey.

text.p: Money managers modestly reduced their duration exposure on their U.S. debt portfolios and raised a little cash over the past week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"After having extended portfolio durations back to basically flat, survey participants raised a little cash and shortened up just slightly in the past week," the report said.
In the week ended July 1, the cash/assets ratio rose to 7.94 percent from 7.74 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 6.10 percent from 5.71 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index slipped to 99.76 percent from 100.01 percent on an arithmetic basis and fell to 98.97 percent from 99.31 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index rose to 4.87 from 4.78 on an arithmetic basis. It inched up to 4.59 from 4.53 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
Four percent of the portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, unchanged from the week ending June 24.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
